question.problem:
Given the **orthonormal** basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $\frac{1}{2}{x}_{1}$, where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{14}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{14}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{14}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{\sqrt{35}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{35}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{35}}\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{10} \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

current_example.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2.$ 

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157829/assets/8f5047a7a26eb24a1a651cbcf809bf7d0923034ca87aa4052e36f0d9501c85c9.svg) where $x_i = \mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i.$ Computing the components of $\mathbf{x},$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-2-6=-8 \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-4+3=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157829/assets/1f4da09e0c3737ab5566d91aec525c48be43a8716dce96dedf0821293689dcac.svg)
